title: Why do birds lay eggs?
examples: Do baby birds eat the yolk?
How long are eggs in the nest?

explain.say: Birds lay eggs to keep their babies safe.

draw.text: Eggs keep babies safe until hatch.

explain.say: The shell around the egg keeps little birds from getting hurt.
Inside the egg, the baby bird gets all the food it needs to grow.

draw.text: Food inside egg helps baby grow.

explain.say: When the baby bird is ready, it uses a small crack to hatch out.

draw.text: Crack helps baby bird hatch out.

explain.say: A real life example is when a mother bird builds a nest.

draw.text: Nest keeps eggs warm and safe.

explain.say: Sometimes people think birds just drop eggs anywhere they want.

draw.text: Birds choose safe spots for eggs.

faq.q: Why do birds lay eggs instead of giving birth?
faq.a: Birds lay eggs because it is how their kind is built to reproduce. They keep the babies safe inside the shell until they hatch.

faq.q: How long does it take for a baby bird to hatch?
faq.a: It depends on the type of bird, but it takes time for the baby to grow enough to break out of the egg.
asks: When do baby birds come out?

faq.q: What keeps the baby bird safe inside the egg?
faq.a: The hard shell around the egg keeps the baby safe from getting hurt by things outside the nest. It is a protective covering.
asks: What protects the baby in the egg?

faq.q: Does the egg give the baby all its food?
faq.a: Yes, the food inside the egg, like the yolk, gives the baby energy to grow until it can eat on its own. This food is stored energy.
asks: Where does the baby get food from?
Can the egg feed the baby?

faq.q: Can birds lay eggs in any place?
faq.a: No, birds usually choose a safe, hidden spot like a nest to lay their eggs. They look for protection first.
asks: Where do birds like to lay eggs?

facts: Bird eggs have a hard outer shell for protection.
The yolk inside the egg provides food for the growing chick.
Birds typically build a nest to keep eggs warm and safe.
Hatching is the process when the baby bird breaks out of the shell.

quiz.say: The main job of the egg shell is to:

options.show: Make the baby bird warm enough.
options.say: Make the baby bird warm enough.

options.show: Give the baby bird all its food.
options.say: Give the baby bird all its food.

options.show: Keep the baby safe from outside harm.
options.say: Keep the baby safe from outside harm.

options.show: Help the baby bird breathe air.
options.say: Help the baby bird breathe air.

quiz.why: The shell acts like a strong, hard covering to protect the fragile life inside.

wrong.0: The nest and the mother keep the baby warm, not just the shell.
wrong.1: The yolk inside the egg provides the food, not the shell itself.
wrong.3: Breathing is done through the shell, but the shell is mainly for physical protection.

quiz.say: What part of the egg gives the baby energy to grow?
quiz.show: Yolk provides food for growing chick.

options.show: The white part around the yolk.
options.say: The white part around the yolk.

quiz.why: The yolk is rich in nutrients and fats, which is the baby's stored food source.

wrong.0: The white part is mostly water, not the main source of energy.
wrong.1: The shell is hard and protective, but it has no food value.
wrong.2: The air pocket helps with gas exchange, but it does not contain food.

quiz.say: If a bird lays an egg, what must it usually do to keep it safe?
quiz.show: Birds must build a nest for safety.

options.show: Lay it in the open dirt.
options.say: Lay it in the open dirt.

options.show: Just leave it on the ground.
options.say: Just leave it on the ground.

options.show: Lay it on a high branch alone.
options.say: Lay it on a high branch alone.

quiz.why: Building a nest keeps the eggs hidden, warm, and safe from dangers.

wrong.0: Open dirt can be too cold or wet for the eggs.
wrong.1: The ground can be dangerous or eaten by other animals.
wrong.3: A high branch might be visible to predators.
